title: Sparse Checkout
description: Use sparse checkout to check out only a subset of files and directories from a large repository.

data.text: Sparse checkout allows you to check out only the files and directories you need, leaving the rest in the Git index without materializing them in your working directory. This is useful for large repositories where you only work on a specific component.
Sparse checkout is configured through the Git core.sparseCheckout setting and a .git/info/sparse-checkout file that lists the paths to include.

data.title: Enable sparse checkout
data.code:
# Step 1: Enable sparse checkout
git config core.sparseCheckout true

# Step 2: Define which paths to include
echo "src/app/" > .git/info/sparse-checkout
echo "src/lib/" >> .git/info/sparse-checkout
echo "README.md" >> .git/info/sparse-checkout

# Step 3: Update the working directory
git read-tree -mu HEAD

# Only src/app/, src/lib/, and README.md
# are materialized in the working directory

data.text: Git 2.25 introduced the git sparse-checkout command, which simplifies the setup process. Use git sparse-checkout init and git sparse-checkout set to configure sparse checkout without manually editing the sparse-checkout file.

data.title: Modern sparse checkout with git sparse-checkout
data.code:
# Initialize sparse checkout
git sparse-checkout init --cone

# Set the directories you want
git sparse-checkout set src/app/ src/lib/

# Add more directories
git sparse-checkout add README.md docs/

# List current sparse checkout patterns
git sparse-checkout list

# Disable sparse checkout (restore all files)
git sparse-checkout disable

# Re-enable with all files
git sparse-checkout set /*

data.text: Combine sparse checkout with partial clone for maximum disk savings. Partial clone gives you full history without file contents; sparse checkout materializes only the files you need.

data.title: Partial clone + sparse checkout
data.code:
# Clone with partial clone and sparse checkout
git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/example/monorepo.git
cd monorepo

# Enable sparse checkout
git sparse-checkout init --cone

# Check out only the packages you need
git sparse-checkout set packages/app/ packages/shared/

# Result:
# - Full commit history available for bisect, log, blame
# - Only app and shared packages materialized on disk

data.text: In CI, sparse checkout reduces the number of files that need to be checked out and built. Combine it with actions/checkout or GitLab's sparse-checkout feature.

data.title: Sparse checkout in GitHub Actions
data.code:
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    sparse-checkout: |
      src/app/
      src/lib/
    sparse-checkout-cone-mode: true

- run: npm install
- run: npm test

data.title: Sparse checkout works for monorepos
data.text: Monorepos with many packages are ideal for sparse checkout. Check out only the package you are building, reducing build time and disk usage.

items.question: Can I commit with sparse checkout?
items.answer: Yes. Sparse checkout only affects which files are materialized. You can stage, commit, and push changes normally.

items.question: What if I need to edit a file outside the sparse checkout?
items.answer: Add its directory to the sparse checkout with git sparse-checkout add <path>. The file will be materialized in the working directory.

items.question: Does sparse checkout affect git diff?
items.answer: git diff only shows changes in materialized files. Files outside the sparse checkout are not shown, even if they are modified in the index.

items.question: Can I use sparse checkout with existing branches?
items.answer: Yes. Sparse checkout applies to the current branch and persists across checkout operations.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: git sparse-checkout init --cone enables modern sparse checkout
git sparse-checkout set <paths> defines which files to materialize
Combine with partial clone for maximum disk savings
Sparse checkout is ideal for monorepos and large repositories
Use actions/checkout sparse-checkout input in CI
